title: Naman Dhir's rise: How the 'jugaadu' cricketer carved his space
content: Naman Dhir's surprise India call-up raised eyebrows but the Punjab all-rounder is beginning to justify the selectors' faith. From contemplating a move to Canada after repeated rejections to impressing with bat and ball, Dhir's journey is one of resilience, adaptability and the unwavering support of his father and late mentor.

title: Why the US midterms matter for Trump & the Democrats - explained in 10 charts
content: Scheduled for November 3, the US midterm elections are poised to significantly influence the current Trump administration. All 435 House seats and 35 Senate positions are up for grabs, making Congressional control pivotal for advancing Trump's policy goals. Voter priorities like the economy, immigration, healthcare, and democracy are expected to heavily sway electoral outcomes, shaping both immediate governance and the political landscape ahead of the 2028 presidential election.

title: Barclays to cut 5,000 jobs, cites AI efficiency; here's what employee presentation said
content: Barclays is initiating a plan to cut around 5,000 jobs primarily due to AI adoption and efficiency increases. The reduction includes about 1,000 positions already eliminated and 4,000 expected by 2026. As a result, the cuts will mainly impact support functions, including software developers, under their cost-saving program. Barclays continues developing its workforce despite the reductions, aiming for improved operational efficiency.

title: Ontario farmer turned down C$16m for 164 acres; 29 acres protected for 999 years
content: Charles Stevens and his family have decided to protect Wilmot Orchards by placing a conservation easement on the property. This easement effectively restricts future development for nearly 1,000 years, ensuring continued agricultural use. Their decision counters pressures from developers seeking to convert farmland into housing. The Stevens family aims to preserve the land for future generations of farmers.

title: Romania blames Russia as drone strike sinks cargo ship in Black Sea; 1 dead, 3 missing
content: In a recent incident near Romania’s Black Sea coast, a drone strike led to the sinking of the Comoros-flagged cargo ship Khoryv. Tragically, one sailor lost his life, and three others are still unaccounted for, raising alarm over regional shipping security. Amid a spate of assaults on vessels, Romania has placed the blame on Russia.

title: New York family blocks road with tree trunks, court awards it to neighbouring club
content: In a landmark ruling, a New York family has lost their claim to a shared private road that now belongs to a nearby recreational club. This road, previously amicably used for decades, became contentious in 2021 when disagreements over access arose. The state’s highest court ultimately sided with the club, citing its historical maintenance and usage, despite the family's assertions of permission based on their long-term relationship.

title: George Washington artwork hidden in folder for 60 years sold for $226,600
content: A remarkable early 19th-century folk art piece, showcasing George Washington, has achieved a staggering auction price of $226,600 after lying dormant for 60 years. This striking artwork embodies the fraktur tradition of Pennsylvania German heritage, adorned with patriotic imagery. The strong interest stemmed from its superb condition and rich historical context, illustrating the enduring passion for distinguished American folk art among collectors and institutions alike.

title: Lauren Conrad bought Beverly Hills penthouse for $1.35m, sold for $2.8m
content: Lauren Conrad, known for The Hills, sold her renovated Beverly Hills penthouse for $2.8 million. She initially purchased the property for $1.35 million four years earlier. After extensive renovations, she transformed the space into a modern home with high-end finishes. The penthouse includes a large open-plan living area, multiple bedrooms, and outdoor terraces. Conrad's real estate ventures in Southern California continue to show significant financial returns.

title: Satya Nadella’s experimental culture loses its home as Microsoft shuts its maker lab
content: Microsoft is shutting down The Garage, its 17-year-old innovation lab and maker space program that ran the company's Global Hackathon. Some Garage spaces across 15 regions, including India, could close from October 23. CEO Satya Nadella regularly attended its hackathons, which produced the Xbox Adaptive Controller and Seeing AI. Employees link the closure to Microsoft's wider cost cuts as it spends heavily on AI infrastructure.

title: UK man's 20-year Spitfire garage project sold for £18,000 after his death
content: Peter Arnold, affectionately dubbed 'Mr Spitfire', dedicated over half a century to amassing historic aircraft relics. After his passing in 2025, a remarkable unfinished Spitfire fuselage went under the hammer for £18,000. This Spitfire F Mk 22 PK519 fuselage featured original components, resting in Arnold's garage for 20 years. Besides the fuselage, auctioned treasures included vintage aircraft instruments and a mesmerizing clock.

title: Andy Murray’s wife Kim Sears and four children: Inside his family life after retirement
content: Andy Murray has officially retired from professional tennis and, in doing so, has opened a new chapter in his life, and the former world No 1 will have more time to spend with his wife Kim Sears and their four children. From parenting and family routines to their shared business interests at Cromlix, the couple are handling life outside the demands of professional tennis while keeping family at the center.

title: Tom Brady donated $170,000 Salem State speaking fee to charities in 2015
content: Tom Brady collected $170,000 for a speaking gig at Salem State University, generously donating the entire sum to charity. He allocated $50,000 to Best Buddies and distributed the remaining funds to various other organizations. With approximately 4,000 attendees present, ticket sales effectively covered his speaking fee. However, the event was notable for Brady facing questions about the NFL's Deflategate saga. The university reported a financial profit from hosting the event.

title: On UP voter list: Ram Ne Yadav Ko Mara, s/o Murkh Chandra Yadav

Notable entries include voters with odd names and details that do not align with reality. The Chief Electoral Officer stated that fewer than 150 inaccuracies were identified among 14.8 lakh registered voters. Despite the digital system's introduction, verification processes remain questioned after complaints from various political parties.

title: DiCaprio-backed group helped buy over 52,000 acres in Chile; protection in talks
content: In 2025, Guafo Island in Chile was acquired with a mission: to safeguard its rich wildlife and thwart harmful development. Collaborative efforts between local partners and authorities are vital in securing legal protections for the island. Engaging indigenous communities in resource negotiations enhances respect for local customs while ensuring a strategic management plan, pivotal for the island's ecological integrity and cultural preservation.

title: Mississippi sinks 31-ton propane tank and steel tower to build fish reef
content: A 31-ton propane tank and steel tower once used for firefighter training in Mississippi have been sunk about 13 miles offshore to create an artificial reef for marine life. Supported by Chevron and local organisations, the project aims to provide shelter for fish and improve fishing opportunities. A similar reef created in 2023 now supports more than 530 red snapper, according to official estimates.

title: Saudi Arabia eyes bigger missiles as Houthi threat meets Iran nuclear fears
content: Recent reports indicate that Saudi Arabia is stepping up its missile production capabilities by developing a new missile complex near Al-Dawadmi. This initiative seems focused on creating solid-fuel missiles, potentially improving the kingdom's defense against threats, particularly from Yemen's Houthi movement. As these advancements unfold, fears about a possible nuclear arms race with Iran grow, especially with the US civilian nuclear cooperation agreement raising concerns over regional nuclear proliferation.

title: New York court upholds wife's $6.83m divorce award involving business stakes
content: In a recent high-profile divorce case, Shirley F. Atkins emerged victorious with a settlement of $6.83 million from James C. Atkins. The appeals court affirmed her entitlement to 22.5% of his business interests and stock sale proceeds. Both sides presented compelling arguments to adjust this percentage. Furthermore, the court ruled on tax responsibilities and payment structures, illustrating its power in equitable asset distribution during divorce proceedings.

title: Rickshaw puller's daughter brings Rs 100 coaching to 7,650 rural children
content: Archana Jaisal established Shiksha Saathi to provide after-school education to children in rural Uttar Pradesh. The initiative also trains local women to become teachers, creating employment opportunities for them. Since its launch, Shiksha Saathi has reached thousands of students across six districts. Women like Neetu now earn a steady income while contributing to their communities' education. The organization continues to empower children and women through accessible educational resources.

title: Chris Pratt's parenting lesson for 4 kids: Start and end each day with faith
content: Chris Pratt opens up about how his faith shapes his parenting, stressing the importance of teaching his kids about Christianity and the significance of prayer. He shares insights from his spiritual path, particularly the lessons learned during his son Jack's health struggles. With a firm belief in passing on his values, Pratt is proud to be open about his faith as he navigates fatherhood.

title: Who is Himanshu Nandal? The swimmer who won three bronze medals at Asian Para Games
content: Himanshu Nandal, a 22-year-old para-swimmer from India, has made history at the Asian Para Games in Japan by winning three bronze medals, including one in the 100m freestyle S11 category. Born with blindness, Nandal’s passion for sports ignited early, and since he began swimming competitively in 2021, he has achieved significant international success, thus shining a light on the extraordinary talents of para athletes in India.

Originally, authorities had denied the request due to security concerns and festival commitments. The concert marks the start of Dosanjh's Aura Tour in India, which includes seven cities. Organisers had multiple meetings with police to finalize security arrangements. The denial of permission earlier faced criticism from political leaders who accused the government of censorship.

Booth clashed with the Efroymson House Owner's Association over alleged vandalism of shared garden spaces, including shrubs, flowers, and lighting. The Indiana Court of Appeals upheld an injunction against Booth, highlighting the HOA's ownership of common areas. Despite Booth's claim of property rights, the court affirmed evidence of his destructive actions, siding with the HOA.

title: Canadian club with 4 members to donate nearly 100 acres for bee research

The donation aims to maintain the land for conservation and research instead of development. The University of Guelph will continue its long-term apiary operation critical to honeybee genetics work.

title: Churchill's 1948 painting sold for £716,800; hammer proceeds to charity
content: Winston Churchill's artwork, Amaryllis Lily, fetched an impressive £716,800 at auction, with proceeds directed toward the Churchill Fellowship. This funding will bolster the Making Space for the Arts initiative, aimed at increasing public participation in the arts. The piece, which has a fascinating legacy, was originally given to Churchill's daughter before being donated. This auction not only exceeded expectations but also empowers the charity to support significant artistic community initiatives.

title: Punjab: Badal praises SAD-BJP rule as Amit Shah’s NDA pitch fuels reunion buzz

title: Three medals in a day! Thulasimathi Murugesan caps Asian Para Games campaign with gold
content: At the Asian Para Games held in Aichi-Nagoya, Thulasimathi Murugesan showcased an exceptional performance by clinching gold in women's doubles and earning two silver medals in other competitions. Nitesh Kumar also shone brightly, winning gold in the men's singles SL3 event and a silver in mixed doubles. India's impressive tally rose to 106 medals across various sports, marking a significant achievement compared to past editions.

The target is to deliver an average of 85 aircraft annually for U.S.

The sixth-ranked flyweight believes the matchup offers an opportunity to strengthen his title credentials. title: Maritime outreach: Navy to host three-day Indo-Pacific Regional Dialogue
content: The Indian Navy will host the 2026 Indo-Pacific Regional Dialogue in New Delhi from November 3rd to 5th. This event will gather naval leaders, policymakers, and maritime experts from 18 countries to discuss cooperation. The conference will focus on science, technology, and academic cooperation while addressing concerns over climate change and maritime security. Special sessions will facilitate exchanges among former naval chiefs and ambassadors about maritime initiatives.

title: MLC polls: Supriya Sule flags spy-cam pen allegations, Devendra Fadnavis responds

Voters were reportedly asked to clip the pens to their pockets, film their ballots and collect money on showing the video. Sule urged the Election Commission to investigate. Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis said he doesn’t know what a spycam pen is. Counting is scheduled for October 27.

title: Florida court orders child support redo after husband's $8,600 bills counted

Bianca Rampartap sought a review after her ex-husband halted his parenting time. The earlier court wrongly counted his financial contributions as income for Bianca, leading her to appeal. The higher court ruled in her favor, requiring a reexamination of her income and subsequent modifications to child support arrangements.

Infrastructure improvements, such as underground shelters along the Line of Actual Control, are underway to enhance troop safety. A substantial budget has been allocated for the modernization of capabilities focused on high-altitude operations. Training programs are designed to prepare personnel for complex border scenarios similar to past clashes.
